affected_system: roadway, bridge, sidewalk, signal, and public right-of-way asset network
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for phased road and bridge preventive maintenance treatment
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of phased road and bridge preventive maintenance treatment
pair matched asset event-study with inspection and traffic panels with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Assets, inspections, defects, work orders, costs, traffic, restrictions, and completion are reconciled.
Engineering thresholds and deterioration models are locally reviewed and versioned.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for phased road and bridge preventive maintenance treatment.

constraints.description: The road and bridge asset management evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: public works asset manager and chief infrastructure engineer
decision_question: Did phased preventive treatments extend verified asset condition and reduce unplanned service loss?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The road and bridge asset management evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.decision_object: phased road and bridge preventive maintenance treatment
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for phased road and bridge preventive maintenance treatment passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: matched asset event-study with inspection and traffic panels
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in verified condition life and unplanned restriction days

intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased road and bridge preventive maintenance treatment, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in verified condition life and unplanned restriction days
distributional gap in change in verified condition life and unplanned restriction days
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer structural safety or causal lifecycle value without comparable inspections and treatment assignment.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for phased road and bridge preventive maintenance treatment passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

title: Evaluate preventive maintenance and treatment strategies
transportability_risks: Materials, climate, loading, standards, inspection, procurement, and unit costs differ.
Service requests can reveal workload but not structural condition or safety.
